newsitem.title: FRANCE: EU export subsidy underpins French wheat.
newsitem.headline: EU export subsidy underpins French wheat.

text.p: French wheat was firmer on Friday, helped by news the European Union has reverted to granting wheat export subsidies for the first time in more than a year, dealers said.
Wheat into Rouen for October-December delivery was quoted at 890-895 francs per tonne, up five on Thursday.
Wheat for January-March delivery was paid at 870 francs, up ten on the previous session.
"The market is reacting to (the EU's) gesture," one trader said.
"The tonnages granted and the amount of the subsidy are encouraging," an other dealer said.
On Thursday the European Union agreed the commercial export of 237,470 tonnes of wheat at a maximum 4.97 Ecus per tonne refund.
Prices are expected to stay firm next week as operators need to cover the recent sale of 450,000 tonnes of French wheat to Egypt, dealers said.
